subject: Business Studies
central_question: How are private, public and global enterprises organised, why has the role of the public sector changed, and how do joint ventures and public-private partnerships combine capabilities?
in_scope_units: Private and public sectors in a mixed economy.
Forms of organising public sector enterprises.
Departmental undertakings: features, merits and limitations.
Statutory corporations: features, merits and limitations.
Government companies: features, merits and limitations.
Changing role of the public sector before and after the 1991 reforms.
Developmental role of public enterprises and disinvestment, sick-unit policy and MoU.
Meaning, types and benefits of joint ventures.
Public Private Partnership model and allocation of responsibilities and risks.
banned_topics: Detailed private-sector forms of organisation, which belong to Chapter 2.
Formation and incorporation procedure of a company, which belongs to Chapter 7.
Detailed sources of business finance, which belong to Chapter 8.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every public enterprise is organised as a government department.
known_pitfalls.correction: Public enterprises may be departmental undertakings, statutory corporations or government companies.

known_pitfalls.claim: A statutory corporation is incorporated under the Companies Act.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is created by a Special Act of Parliament that defines its powers and functions.

known_pitfalls.claim: Any company with some government investment is a government company.
known_pitfalls.correction: Not less than 51 per cent of paid-up capital must be held by the specified government or governments, including qualifying subsidiaries.

known_pitfalls.claim: Disinvestment necessarily means immediate closure of a public enterprise.
known_pitfalls.correction: Disinvestment is sale of government equity to the public or private sector; closure is a separate decision for units that cannot be revived.

known_pitfalls.claim: A joint venture always creates a new company.
known_pitfalls.correction: A contractual joint venture creates no jointly owned entity, while an equity-based joint venture does.

recommended_example_progression: Use Short Answer Question 3 to classify public-sector organisations.
Use Long Answer Question 2 to explain the role of the public sector before 1991.
Use Long Answer Question 1 to analyse Industrial Policy 1991 toward public enterprises.
Use Long Answer Question 4 to evaluate the strength of global enterprises.
Use Long Answer Question 5 to compare benefits of joint ventures and PPP.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end section contains Short Answer Questions 1–7, Long Answer Questions 1–5 and a project on Indian companies entering joint ventures with foreign companies.
